stem: Based on the excerpt, why were Muhammad Ali’s actions significant?

options.label: A
options.text: He discouraged ordinary citizens from taking a stance against the war.

options.label: B
options.text: He used controversies about the war to draw attention to sporting events he was involved in.

options.label: C
options.text: He brought attention to the anti-war movement at great personal risk.

options.label: D
options.text: He encouraged other athletes to boycott their sport as a form of protest against the war.

visual_elements: The [draftee] drawing such intense interest was Muhammad Ali, the undefeated heavyweight champion of the world. Over the past three years, Ali had become a national [outcast] for his views on race, religion, and especially the Vietnam War. . . . . . He was tried and convicted of draft evasion in federal district court and sentenced to the maximum penalty. He was stripped of his [boxing] titles and suspended from boxing during the peak of his career, losing millions of dollars in the process. . . . In response, Ali and his legal team launched a lengthy challenge against his conviction that ended with victory in the Supreme Court of the United States in 1971. —Winston Bowman, "United States v. Clay: Muhammad Ali’s Fight against the Vietnam Draft," 2018
